resale_co.name: Residential Resale Continued Certificate of Occupancy / Dwelling Certificate
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Woodland Park Department of Inspections (Code Enforcement / Construction Code Enforcing Agency), under Borough Ordinances 14-14 and 22-50.2
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are Monday to Friday, 10 am to 12 pm once the paperwork is complete; the water meter compliance application must reach the Water office at least 2 weeks before closing
requirements: Walkways not broken or lifted; exterior stairs in good condition with handrails; interior stairs with handrails
Roof, gutters and leaders in good condition; exterior paint at least fair; no broken window glass
Street number posted on or close to the door
Garbage removed, overgrowth cut back, no unregistered vehicles or car parts stored on the property
Smoke detectors on each level and within 10 feet of bedrooms; carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of bedrooms (separate Fire Prevention certificate required first)
Dead bolts on exterior doors must have inside thumb latches (no double-keyed locks)
Basement kitchens or bathrooms built without a permit must be removed
Plumbing waste and supply lines in good condition and not leaking; sump pump must drain outside, not into the sewer
Heating equipment and water heaters properly vented into the chimney; water heater relief valve extension to within 12 inches of the floor
Septic systems: a licensed professional must certify the system works and meets DEP rules (resale only)
Open permits must be closed out before the certificate is issued
Water meter compliance sign-off from DPW (wireless reading meter if on Woodland Park water)
Photo ID of the buyer and a list of all occupants (Dwelling Certificate) with IDs
The 2026 checklist still says fire extinguishers are required to meet NJ Division of Fire Safety rules

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Residential Resale packet from the Borough's Residential C.O. Forms page. Fill out the resale application and the Dwelling Certificate listing all occupants with photo IDs, file the Water Meter Compliance Application with the Water office at 5 Brophy Lane at least 2 weeks before closing, and file the separate Fire Prevention application. Pay with two separate checks payable to the Borough of Woodland Park (one for the certificate of occupancy, one for fire), or cash; no debit or credit cards. Call Code Enforcement at 973-345-8100 ext 103 for the inspection.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Code Official/Bldg. Subcode Official/Bldg. Inspector/Code Enforcement Officer/Zoning Official

evidence.quote: Continued Certificate of Occupancy /Dwelling Certificate Pursuant to Borough Ordinances 22-50.2 & 14.14 RESIDENTIAL RESALE
Borough of Woodland Park Ordinance 14-14 requires a new Certificate of Occupancy prior to the sale of all residential property and/or the rental of a residential home or apartment.

For the resale of a one- or two-family dwelling, in addition to a certificate of occupancy, a smoke detector/carbon monoxide detector certificate must be obtained from the Fire Official's office. A certificate of occupancy cannot be issued unless and until the certification has been obtained and copy provided to the Code Enforcement office.
This application MUST be submitted to the Water office (Mon-Fri, 8:30am to 4:30pm) located at 5 Brophy Lane, Woodland Park, NJ AT LEAST 2 WEEKS PRIOR to the closing date and/or any occupancy change.
We need two separate checks, both made payable to the Borough of Woodland Park. We take cash as well, no debit or credit cards.

We also check if there are any open permits and they need to be closed out/inspected before the CO is issued. Once the paperwork is satisfied, we can schedule our inspection which is done Monday-Friday from 10-12.
Call Code Enforcement at 973-345-8100 ext 103 for an appointment for any type of Inspection
Burghardt, Allan Construction Code Official/Bldg. Subcode Official/Bldg. Inspector/Code Enforcement Officer/Zoning Official 973-345-8100 x103 973-345-3729 (fax) aburghardt@wpnj.us

resale_co.notes: The Residential Resale packet (scanned, March 2026) requires a Continued Certificate of Occupancy / Dwelling Certificate on every residential sale (Ordinances 14-14 and 22-50.2). The two-family fee is inconsistent inside the packet: the application page says 2-Family Fee $200.00, while the procedures and fees page says $100.00 for the resale of a one- or two-family home (the cover letter lists 1 family rental/resale $100.00). Both are recorded; confirm with Code Enforcement. The cover letter also gives Allan Burghardt's office line as (973) 345-8100 ext:208, while the Department of Inspections page and the staff directory give ext. 103. Code Enforcement/Zoning Inspector: Marvin Moran (x224 on the department page, mmoran@wpnj.us); Secretary/Technical Assistant: Gina Valentin (x209, codeenforcement@wpnj.us). Rentals need the same certificate ($100.00 per unit) plus, for homes built before 1978, a lead-safe certificate and proof of liability insurance; those are rental items, not resale items. The packet's checklist still lists fire extinguishers even though the state dropped them from the state smoke certificate in February 2025.

requirements: Battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units (since 1/1/2019); hardwired 110V smoke alarms and CO alarms no more than 10 years old
Hardwired interconnected smoke alarms must work and cannot be replaced by battery alarms; alarm systems with a keypad need the code and monitoring company number at the inspection
Smoke and CO alarms on all floors with sleeping areas (including the basement), within 10 feet of sleeping areas; smoke alarms at least 4 inches from the wall or ceiling
Bedrooms directly off the kitchen need the alarm inside the bedroom, not in the kitchen
CO alarm on any level with an attached garage or a gas-fired device (stove, boiler, dryer, fireplace)
Homes with a secondary power source need 'CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER' marking within 18 inches of the main panel and electric meter
Someone over 18 must be present; the full fee is due with the application before an inspection is scheduled

fire_cert.notes: Fees come from the Bureau's one-two family application (created March 17, 2025): $50.00, $100.00 or $150.00 by how soon the inspection is wanted; the Borough's 2026 CO cover letter repeats the same three tiers. A failed $50 inspection needs a new application and fee; the $100 and $150 tiers include one free re-inspection, after which a new application and fee are needed. The Bureau's phone appears both as (973) 345-8100 x106 (Fire Prevention page and CO procedures sheet) and (973) 345-3899 (application form, staff directory and state directory). Fire Inspectors: Sam Gaita, Sr (x243) and Gerald Walis (x241). The 2025 fire application does not list a fire extinguisher. The West Paterson / Woodland Park volunteer fire department (Chief Paul Salomone Jr) handles emergency response.

other_items.label: Water meter compliance (DPW sign-off)
other_items.detail: File the Water Meter Compliance Application at the Water office, 5 Brophy Lane, at least 2 weeks before closing; homes on Woodland Park water need wireless meter reading, and DPW sign-off must be shown to Code Enforcement before the certificate is granted (DPW 973-256-1264).

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: Any open permits must be closed out and inspected before the certificate of occupancy is issued.

other_items.label: Septic certification (resale only)
other_items.detail: A licensed professional must certify that a septic system works properly and meets DEP requirements.
